 Fidlock Recalls Hermetic Dry Bags in the US Over Magnets That Could Detach and Cause Serious Injuries
 Fidlock recalls 490 Hermetic Dry Bags in the US over magnets that can detach and cause serious injuries. Check the affected lot and how to get a refund.
 Abel Ruiz 
 November 20, 2026, 11:13 AM

 A manufacturing defect in the magnetic closure of Fidlock Hermetic waterproof bags has triggered a US safety recall involving hundreds of units. The problem could cause small magnets to separate from the bags, creating a potentially life-threatening ingestion hazard, particularly for children. The affected batch had already been recalled in several international markets before the latest US announcement .
 Fidlock Hermetic Dry Bag. Image: Fidlock Approximately 490 waterproof bags recalled over defective magnetic closures
 The US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) announced the recall on November 19, 2026, affecting approximately 490 Fidlock Hermetic Dry Bags sold nationwide . The agency identified a manufacturing defect in the adhesive bonding that secures the magnetic closure strips to the bag. These strips can partially or completely detach, potentially releasing the magnets embedded inside.
 The danger goes beyond the loss of the bag's waterproof seal. If two or more powerful magnets are swallowed, they can attract each other through intestinal tissue or become attached to another metal object inside the digestive tract. This can lead to intestinal perforations, blockages, infections, and potentially fatal complications. The CPSC reports that no incidents or injuries have been reported in connection with the US recall.

 The affected product is the Fidlock Hermetic Dry Bag Medi, specifically lot number 2409140930201 . It is a transparent, medium-sized waterproof bag measuring approximately 8 inches tall and 4.6 inches wide. The bag features a blue magnetic closure strip, a black lanyard, and the Fidlock name printed in white across the front of the closure. The lot number appears on the back of the strip. The product's item number is D-11111A-F0000(PTTT), and its barcode is 4251207401183.
 The recalled bags were sold between January 2025 and September 2026 at sporting goods, watersports, and outdoor retailers across the United States, as well as through Fidlock.us and Amazon.com. Prices ranged from $30 to $35 . Only products bearing the identified lot number are included in this recall. Other Hermetic bags and Fidlock magnetic accessories are not covered by the CPSC announcement.
 The same manufacturing defect prompted earlier recalls overseas
 Although the CPSC announcement was issued on November 19, the affected batch had already drawn attention from product safety authorities outside the United States. The United Kingdom issued an official recall notice on September 10, 2026, identifying the same defective adhesive bond and the risk posed by exposed magnets. France also registered a recall involving the same model and lot number.
 The product has also appeared in the European Union's Safety Gate alert system, which allows participating countries to exchange information about potentially dangerous consumer products. These earlier actions establish that the manufacturing defect extends beyond the approximately 490 units covered by the latest US recall. However, the figures published by individual authorities should not be combined without confirming whether they refer to separate inventories.
 The international notifications also highlight an important distinction: the recall concerns one specific manufacturing batch, not Fidlock's magnetic closure technology as a whole . Owners should check the lot number rather than assuming that every Hermetic waterproof bag is affected.
 How US customers can request a replacement or refund
 Fidlock is instructing consumers to stop using affected Hermetic Dry Bag Medi products immediately and keep them out of children's reach . Customers can receive a replacement bag or a gift card for the Fidlock USA online store. Those who purchased directly from the company's online store may instead qualify for a full refund to their original credit card or PayPal account.
 To begin the process, US customers should visit the official Fidlock product recall page and follow the instructions for submitting photographic documentation. The company asks consumers to provide evidence of the affected product before disposing of it. Owners should keep the bag and any loose magnets inaccessible to children while arranging the recall remedy.

 Consumers can also contact Fidlock USA at 888-303-8332 , Monday through Friday, from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern Time, or by email at recall_2608@fidlock.com. Additional information, including the official product identification and recall number 27-093, is available in the CPSC recall announcement .
 The safety alert does not involve other magnetic products recently introduced by the German manufacturer, including the Fidlock Pinclip Battery Light system . Those bicycle lights use a separate magnetic-mechanical mounting design and are not part of the Hermetic Dry Bag recall.
